calls.reason: CRS confirms the absence of broad federal AI regulation, supporting the main comparison with state protections. GAO documents narrower federal statutes, so the claim that action consisted only of executive orders overstates the case.

The LawAI paper discusses potential compliance costs but measures neither costs for trillion-dollar companies nor effects on US-China competition. It cannot settle the forecast or its hedged competitive outcome.
Cambridge and CRS describe substantially broader national AI obligations in China. Stanford reports benchmark gaps shrinking to near parity in 2024, supporting progress despite those regulations.

LMArena reports Gemini sweeping its arenas, while Artificial Analysis places Kling first in image-to-video. These category leaders provide mixed evidence without enough ranking coverage to establish national dominance.
Ars reports substantial OpenAI losses, while The Decoder reports Midjourney profitability. Neither establishes aggregate generative-AI net income, leaving the broader financial claim unclear.
